findings.text: The first paragraph says plainly what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves. A newcomer can answer "what is it" and "why does it matter" before scrolling.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. … It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: Near the top, a link jumps to concrete next steps: clone, prerequisites, `./setup.sh`, and an `athena ask "add a changelog"` example. "What to do next" is easy to find and easy to act on.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself.

findings.text: The project's home URL is titled after a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who expects Athena's homepage may think they landed on the wrong page until they read the lede.
findings.source:
/

Athena explains how firstmate handles work

findings.text: The demo is a read-only study of another codebase. It never shows the main thing the lede promises: a request turned into a commit, with the cost and the checking model's verdict. A newcomer sees no example of that output.
findings.source: It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: Most of the page is a detailed state machine of firstmate's internals (12 transition cards, 45 claims). A newcomer evaluating Athena gets little from it beyond seeing that every statement is traced to a source.
findings.source: Headings "States of a piece of work", "Counters", "Transitions", "Why it is built this way", "Claims and sources"

findings.text: This header link speaks to the repository owner ("your decision"). For a newcomer it is confusing and is not a next step.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: The prerequisites list a C linker for a Rust project but do not say whether a Rust toolchain is needed or whether setup.sh installs one. A newcomer may not be sure the list is complete.
findings.source: Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm (to install Claude Code).

findings.text: Jargon such as captain, yolo, green and in scope is defined twice, once in "Words used first" and again in the Glossary. Even so, one key term is admitted to be undefined, which adds load for a first-time reader.
findings.source: <dt>in scope</dt><dd>… The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it.

findings.text: The Limits section openly says the first pass missed several paths and that nothing was run. That is honest. But on a showcase page it may lower a newcomer's confidence in the tool's reading ability.

findings.text: The "About this page" section and the footer refer to internal repository paths. They mean nothing to a newcomer who has not cloned the repository.
findings.source: This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from.
